rows.note: Use 喐 as the all-purpose colloquial verb when a person or thing changes position or posture on its own.
Use 搬 for changing residence or physically carrying and relocating an object.

example.english: I'm going to move to Kowloon next month.
example.jyutping: ngo5 haa6 go3 jyut6 zau6 bun1 heoi3 gau2 lung4

rows.note: Use 推 for the slice of causing something to move by pushing, including when a force pushes it.

example.english: Help me move this table by pushing it aside.
example.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 teoi1 hoi1 zoeng1 toi4

rows.note: Use this for a practiced dance, sports, exercise, or fighting move.

example.english: This dance move is hard to do.
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 mou5 dou6 dung6 zok3 hou2 naan4 zou6

rows.note: Use this for a board-game move, or metaphorically for a strategic move.

example.english: This move gave my opponent a headache.
example.traditional: 呢一步棋令對手好頭痛。
example.jyutping: ni1 jat1 bou6 kei4 ling6 deoi3 sau2 hou2 tau4 tung3

rows.note: For ordinary physical movement, this is the all-purpose one.

example.english: I wake up as soon as I see the cat move.
example.traditional: 我一見到隻貓郁動就醒喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 gin3 dou2 zek3 maau1 juk1 dung6 zau6 seng2 laa3

rows.note: Use this for the event of moving from one home to another.

example.english: We plan to move house next month.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 haa6 go3 jyut6 zau6 bun1 uk1 laa3

rows.note: Use 感動 when something arouses tenderness, compassion, or another strong feeling in someone.

example.english: The movie's ending can really move people.
example.traditional: 套戲個結局真係好感動人。
example.jyutping: tou3 hei3 go3 git3 guk6 zan1 hai6 hou2 gam2 dung6 jan4
